notes:
Summary: Lodestar runs a high-volume adtech stack with two tight latency tiers: (1) real-time bidding assistant/chat for ops (<100ms p95 target), (2) nightly reranking/embedding generation for audience matching (high throughput). They want a Dedicated contract with clear throughput guarantees and an SLA tied to latency percentiles. Procurement oriented toward 12–24 month commit.

Key quotes: "We can’t afford tail latency in the bidding path — p95 must be under 100ms; p99 ideally <200ms." — Head of ML ops.

POC ask: multi-week test on 8x H100-equivalent reserved pool with synthetic RTB traffic + production traces. Validate continuous-batching and KV cache improvements. Must demonstrate 60% baseline utilization and safe burst to 90% for sale days.

Procurement constraints: strict data residency for EU/NA customers, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 type II required. Looking for on-prem option for most-sensitive PII subsets.

Notes on SLA/throughput: want explicit per-route throughput floor (requests/sec) and token TPS guarantees; automatic fallback to hosted model acceptable but with defined latency delta and failover RTO < 3 minutes. They requested query-level tracing and token-level cost breakdown in Console.

Internal risk: legal wants clearer indemnity on model hallucinations for policy-signals models; security wants HSM/KMS diagrams.

Short-term goal: finalize sizing + committed GPU count and baseline monthly price to run procurement by May.

Contact cadence: weekly sync (Maya), ad-hoc infra deep-dive w/ Carlos.
use_case_summary: Primary: low-latency chat assistant for bid ops (p95 <100ms), Secondary: offline reranking and embeddings for audience matching. Also want a fallback routing policy for capacity events and a mixed-hosted/dedicated deployment plan.
cost_model_summary:
Draft TCO provided to Lodestar on 2026-02-27 with three commitment tiers. Assumptions below are the ones discussed on call and in spreadsheet (drive link).

Commit tiers (examples):
- Small commit: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved (12-month); list price baseline $48k/mo. Assumed utilization: 55% baseline, burst to 85% on peak. Effective unit cost: ~$0.0000065 per token at 55% util (chat mix, 4-token avg response).
- Mid commit: 16x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved (12-month); list price baseline $170k/mo. Assumed utilization: 65% baseline, burst to 90%. Effective unit cost: ~$0.0000021 per token at 65% util.
- Large commit: 48x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved (24-month); list price baseline $470k/mo. Assumed utilization: 70% baseline, burst to 92%. Effective unit cost: ~$0.0000011 per token at 70% util.

On-demand comparison: similar workload on hosted API estimated ~$0.000010–0.000012 per token (no commit) — Lodestar sees 3–9x savings with mid/large commit at target utilization.

Break-even analysis: with mid commit (~16 GPUs) breakeven vs on-demand at ~45% utilization. Above 65% utilization yields substantial savings and justifies 12-month commit.

Bursting: recommended burst pool pricing (pay-for-burst) with soft cap; their blocker is how burst is metered and invoiced. Need to clarify whether burst tokens billed at blended commit rate or a higher on-demand uplift.

Model/infra notes: unit economics assume quantized model variants for reranking (int8) and fp16 for chat. KV cache reduces token accounting by ~18% in our sim; includes continuous batching improvements for p95 latency.

Deliverables requested: detailed per-route token cost sheet, GPU mapping (model->GPU), SLA draft with p50/p95/p99 latency commitments and credits schedule, and explicit burst metering language.
technical_requirements:
Latency SLOs: p95 chat <100ms, p99 <250ms; Throughput: sustained 1,200 req/s on chat route during peak, nightly batch 200M tokens window. Reserved GPU planning: map large LLM serving to H100-equivalent counts; want hot KV cache and 2 regional replicas for failover. Need KMS integration and audit logs for tenancy.

Acceptance criteria for POC: sustained p95 under 100ms for 30m window at 65% utilization, successful failover to secondary region within 3 min, and consistent unit-cost reporting in Console.
